interest: This file offers an illuminating micro-historical view of how deteriorating U.S.-Japanese diplomatic relations in the late summer of 1941 directly impacted local American businesses. Following the freezing of Japanese assets in July 1941, routine horticultural trade—such as Easter lily bulbs harvested and awaiting export in Japan—was halted, leaving commercial florists facing severe supply shortages. The file illustrates how constituents petitioned their congressional representatives to lobby the State Department for commercial relief just months before the outbreak of war in the Pacific, while the letterhead provides an incidental record of the House Democratic Steering Committee leadership under Speaker Sam Rayburn.
overview: This file (decimal 894.612/20) from late August and early September 1941 concerns constituent and congressional inquiries regarding the importation of Japanese lily bulbs into the United States. Representative William T. Byrne of New York wrote to Fletcher Warren, Executive Assistant to the Assistant Secretary of State, on behalf of Albany florist William C. Gloeckner, inquiring whether harvested bulbs packed in Japan could be admitted to prevent a shortage of lilies for American florists during the upcoming Easter season. The file includes Byrne's initial inquiry letter, an illegible enclosure page, and Byrne's follow-up letter of September 2, 1941, acknowledging the State Department's reply of August 30, 1941.

subfiles.about: Representative William T. Byrne requests State Department advice on whether harvested Japanese lily bulbs can be admitted into the United States.
subfiles.summary: Representative William T. Byrne writes to Fletcher Warren, Executive Assistant to the Assistant Secretary of State, forwarding a complaint from Albany florist William C. Gloeckner. Gloeckner reported that Japanese lily bulbs had already been harvested and packed for U.S. shipment, warning that an import embargo would leave florists without lilies for the upcoming Easter season. Byrne asks whether any administrative steps can be taken to permit the entry of these ready shipments into the United States.
subfiles.title: Letter from Representative William T. Byrne to Fletcher Warren on Japanese lily bulb imports

The substantive textual content of the page cannot be recovered from the surviving image.

subfiles.about: Representative William T. Byrne thanks Fletcher Warren for his August 30 letter regarding Japanese lily bulb imports.
subfiles.summary: Writing on Democratic Steering Committee stationery, Representative William T. Byrne acknowledges and expresses gratitude for Fletcher Warren's letter of August 30 concerning the importation of Japanese lily bulbs. The letter concludes their brief correspondence regarding potential relief for domestic florists. The margin features the names of key Democratic House leaders of the 77th Congress.
